correctness.rationale: The original main mathematics checks out. The exact beta-integral entry differs from x^b/(x+y)^{b+1} at x=j+1,y=k+1 by a bound O_b(x^{b−1}/(x+y)^{b+1}+x^b/(x+y)^{b+2}); each squared bound sums in y to O_b(x^{−3}). The same bounds hold uniformly within cells for the derivatives, proving Hilbert–Schmidt comparison. Under log conjugacy k(u)=e^{(b+1/2)u}(1+e^u)^{−b−1} acts by k(s−t), giving the stated beta symbol with the negative Fourier exponent. Off zero the added complement is invertible, so the scalar positive-half-line index equals the increasing-frequency winding with this convention. At zero, squared column norms are O_b((k+1)^{−1}) and the columns are images of a weakly null unit sequence. The original auxiliary norm discussion should not infer the exact matrix norm from a compact comparison; the independent norm theorem gives the asserted equality. In the repaired proof, independently checked the reflection normalization π/(m! cosh(πξ)), the unwrapped angle and its unattained endpoint −mπ/2, and the locally uniformly convergent derivative of the tail logarithm in the Euler product. Ratio monotonicity allows only ±ξ pairs. Their distinct negative-angle multiples produce exactly the stated number, signs and magnitudes, including zero crossings for m=1,2 and exclusion of the common endpoint at zero. At a crossing, z′(−ξ)=−conjugate(z′(ξ)); the nonzero radial and angular components exclude parallel tangents. The revised files consistently restrict the new claim to this classification and state which results are inputs.
residual_risks: The checker is finite corroboration and was not executed. The repaired theorem is analytic and makes no complete-spectrum or real noninteger crossing claim.

value.rationale: Value of the repair was reassessed independently of the known boundary or index. The nonzero crossings are the singular points where different boundary arcs meet; knowing when they first appear, that all are transverse and real, and their increasing count with m gives global information for interpreting the geometry and winding regions of a natural operator family. Positive integers are a substantive entire family where gamma recurrence yields a finite phase sum, not a short chosen list. The beta boundary alone does not identify these points or even rule out nonreal or tangent intersections. The earlier boundary and classical index are not credited as new value.
